one-line thesis: HCG sharpened its strategic focus by divesting the fertility business (Milann) to concentrate purely on oncology, while delivering 15% FY26 revenue growth and 70bps margin expansion driven by volume growth and payor mix optimization. The successful INR425cr rights issue reduced net debt to 1.4x EBITDA, funding a 200-bed brownfield expansion pipeline aimed at sustaining double-digit growth and targeting 20% ROCE medium-term.
financial scorecard: Revenue: INR652cr (Q4, +11.3% YoY), INR2,545cr (FY26, +15% YoY); EBITDA: INR125cr (Q4, +17% YoY, 19.2% margin), INR471.1cr (FY26, +19% YoY, 18.5% margin); PAT: Not explicitly broken out in transcript text but implied via margin expansion; Order Book: N/A (Service sector); Net Debt: Reduced to 1.4x EBITDA (from 2.2-2.3x); One-offs: ESOP settlement impacted CFO conversion (normalized 87% vs reported 75%); Low-margin business intentionally pared down impacting Q4 topline.
guidance: Revenue Growth: ~15% medium-term; Margin: Confident in continued expansion (targeting ~100bps in FY27); Order Inflow: Driven by 23 new oncologists added in Q4; Capex: INR90-100cr for 200 brownfield beds over 24 months.
order book & pipeline: N/A for hospital services; Pipeline includes 200+ brownfield beds (Cuttack +75, Ranchi +30, Vizag +50, Bhavnagar +20) over 24 months; 8-10 new Day-Care centers planned; 1,000 total bed addition target by FY30 (400 greenfield, 600 brownfield).
segment / subsidiary detail: West Cluster: 45% of revenue, +14% FY26 growth; South Cluster: 39% of revenue, +13% FY26 growth (Q4 moderated by MVT softness); East Cluster: 11% of revenue, +11% FY26 growth; International (Kenya): +71% FY26 revenue growth.
growth verticals / optionality: Brownfield expansions in high-utilization centers (Ahmedabad at 50% utilization); Greenfield pipeline evaluating 10-12 cities (Pune, Surat, Coimbatore, etc.); Doubling Day-Care centers; Clinical talent addition (23 oncologists in Q4); Medical Value Travel recovery initiatives.
margins & cost dynamics: EBITDA margin expanded 70bps FY26 to 18.5% (Q4 up 90bps to 19.2%); Drivers: Operating leverage, better utilization, throughput optimization, payor mix improvement (100bps shift in last 2 quarters); Cost levers: Procurement efficiencies, lease renegotiations; Intentional exit from low-margin business to improve realization.
capex / expansion: INR90-100cr allocated for 200 brownfield beds over next 24 months (avg INR45 lakh/bed); MR-Linac at North Bangalore on pay-per-use (asset-light); Rights issue proceeds (INR425cr) earmarked for capacity expansion, tech upgrades, and selective growth.
capital allocation: Strategic divestiture of Milann (Fertility) for INR37.6cr equity consideration (75% upfront) to focus on core oncology; Rights issue of INR425cr completed to strengthen balance sheet; Debt repayment executed to reduce leverage to 1.4x; Internal net debt/EBITDA ceiling set at 2.5x.
risks & watch-items: Medical Value Travel (MVT) volatility due to geopolitical tensions (Middle East conflict); Execution risk on brownfield expansions; Competition from large multi-specialty chains entering oncology; Regulatory changes in healthcare pricing.
management quality / tone: Confident, disciplined, and strategically focused; Emphasis on 'profitable growth' over pure topline chasing; Transparent on intentional revenue trade-offs for margin quality; Bullish on clinical differentiation as a moat.
non-obvious takeaways: Center utilization (58%) is a blended metric (chemo beds, OT, radiation machines) rather than just bed occupancy, indicating significant headroom in assets like Ahmedabad (50% utilization); ESOP settlement distorted cash flow conversion; MR-Linac deployed on pay-per-use to preserve capital efficiency.
challenges → beneficiaries & losers:
| Challenge | Beneficiary/Loser | Dir | Conviction | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Consolidation of oncology focus and margin expansion via mix shift | HealthCare Global Enterprises Ltd | beneficiary | High | Direct beneficiary of divestiture proceeds, de-leveraged balance sheet, and focused capital deployment into high-return oncology assets. |
| Loss of scale and potential margin pressure from low-margin business exit | Milann Fertility (Divested Entity) | loser | High | Entity sold to Inviga Healthcare Fund; no longer part of HCG consolidated metrics. |

themes.title: Hospitals, diagnostics & domestic healthcare
themes.need: Under-bedded India plus insurance penetration and preventive-care adoption drive a domestic healthcare capex + volume cycle distinct from export pharma. MAXHEALTH adding ~2,500+ beds (Gurgaon 500-bed by FY27); APOLLOHOSP/MEDANTA/KIMS/NH/ASTERDM/MAXHEALTH on hospitals; LALPATHLAB/METROPOLIS/THYROCARE/VIJAYA on diagnostics (LALPATHLAB guides 13-15% FY27); MEDPLUS/ENTERO on pharmacy/distribution; POLYMED on devices. The same India-only demand engine now also carries India-facing branded pharma, which is driven by domestic volume and price rather than the export book: GLAXO delivered its first INR 1,000cr quarter with 8.1% revenue growth, Shingrix at a ~INR 75cr annual run-rate (CY25, +80% YoY) and Jemperli's first-line approval expanding eligible patients from 800 to 6,000; ERIS (dermatology 15% of revenue after INR 1,265cr of domestic brand acquisitions), SANOFI (India-for-India, NLEM price cuts) and THEMISMED (hospital segment +20% YoY) sit on the same axis.
themes.driver: New-bed commissioning + occupancy ramp; Tier 3/4 diagnostics penetration; CGHS rate revision; preventive-test volumes; domestic branded-formulation volume growth and NLEM/price actions.

business_model.title: Positioning (investor deck)
business_model.body:
- "Largest oncology-focused hospital chain with a pan-India network"; the About Us section calls HCG "the largest provider of cancer care in India" through a network of 26 hospitals across India and Kenya.
- Claims leading positions in 16 of 19 cities covered (deck notes: "HCG in top 3 based on management estimates", excluding Chennai), spanning 19 cities / 10 states excluding Kenya.
- Positioned as the "Preferred destination for leading oncologists": full-time and exclusive oncologists, integrated medical/surgical/radiation teams, organ-specific teams, 450+ revenue-generating oncologists and 88% doctor retention rate in FY26.
- Claims a "TRACK RECORD OF BEING 1st TO LAUNCH ADVANCED TECHNOLOGY IN INDIA" (Cyberknife, Tomotherapy, Radixact, Ethos/adaptive radiation, MR-LINAC dated 2026), backed by 1000+ papers published till date and 30+ new clinical trials in FY2026.
- Multi-disciplinary Tumor Board approach run weekly nation-wide for 17+ years, with 250+ oncologists participated and 36K+ cases discussed till date.

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Divestment] "Completed Strategic Exit from Milann" — the fertility business was divested in June 26 (deck states the sale completed on 29th June, 2026), to sharpen focus on core oncology; it contributed revenue of INR 169 Mn and EBITDA of INR 23 Mn in Q1 FY27.
- [Shareholding] As on 30th June 2026: Promoters 64%, Domestic Institutional Investors 19%, Foreign Institutional Investors 3%, Public 14%.
- [Leadership/Governance] "Management Team Strengthened — Leadership team fully on-boarded"; board includes founder Dr. BS Ajai Kumar (Non-Executive Chairman), Dr Manish Mattoo (Executive Director and CEO) and two KKR nominees (Akshay Tanna, Partner; Simrun Mehta, Managing Director).
- [Provision] An "EPCG-related provision of INR 45.9 Mn" was recognised in Q1 FY27 and is excluded from the deck's Adjusted EBITDA, as are North Bangalore start-up losses of INR 70 Mn.
- [International] International business (Kenya operations, included in consolidated metrics) reported revenue of INR 208 Mn in Q1FY27, ~9% YoY growth, "driven by stronger patient inflows for radiation oncology and PET cases".
